categories.name: Recording
categories.intro: Record the consult on the computer, or import audio from a phone, dictaphone or call app, and nothing is lost if the power goes.

items.name: One-button recording with a live waveform
items.benefit: One large red button starts and stops the recording, and the waveform shows the microphone is hearing you.
items.detail: The round button is 64px (72px on touch screens) and shows a breathing ring, a 48-bar rolling waveform and the elapsed time while recording. The breathing ring is the only animation in the app that never stops.

items.name: Space bar starts and stops recording
items.benefit: With your hands busy, you can start or stop recording from the keyboard.
items.detail: When the Recorder has focus, Space toggles recording. The button can't be pressed while recording is starting or stopping, so a double press can't happen.
items.evidence: apps/desktop/src/screens/Recorder.tsx onKeyDown; packages/ui/src/RecordButton.test.tsx 'can't be pressed while starting or stopping'

items.name: Live transcript while you talk
items.benefit: The transcript builds during the consult, so it is finished the moment you press stop.
items.detail: Voice detection, speech recognition and speaker labelling run while you talk. On a 9.6-minute test consult played in real time, the transcript was complete 0.0 s after stop.

items.name: Live speaker labels
items.benefit: The transcript shows who said what as the consult happens, so the vet's findings stand apart from the owner's history.
items.detail: Each utterance's voice fingerprint (WeSpeaker ResNet34) is matched to the speakers heard so far, and utterances under 1 s never start a new speaker. Across four test consults, 98 to 100% of speech went to the right speaker.
items.evidence: engine/os-engine/src/live.rs DEFAULT_SPEAKER_THRESHOLD (0.65); engine/os-diar/src/lib.rs MIN_EMBED_SECS; docs/perf/M0.md 'Live recording' table ('purity 98-100% across all four fixtures')

items.name: Record from the browser version
items.benefit: The browser version on the same computer records from the microphone too, and explains how to fix a blocked microphone.
items.detail: The browser sends 16 kHz mono audio to the local engine as you speak, with live speaker labels. If microphone permission was denied, a message explains how to allow it again.

items.name: Any microphone, on every desktop system
items.benefit: Use the clinic's preferred USB microphone instead of the laptop's built-in one.
items.detail: Settings lists every input device with a System default option. Capture uses each system's own audio layer: WASAPI on Windows, CoreAudio on macOS, ALSA or PulseAudio on Linux.
items.evidence: engine/os-asr/src/capture.rs; engine/os-cli/src/record.rs (openbark devices); apps/desktop/src/screens/Settings.tsx Recording group

items.name: Crash-safe, encrypted recording
items.benefit: If the computer crashes or loses power mid-consult, everything recorded up to that moment is kept.
items.detail: Audio is written to disk as it is recorded, already encrypted, and a cut-off recording is repaired so all of it can still be read. The status line tells you the audio is saved as you go.

items.name: Screen stays on while recording
items.benefit: The screen doesn't go dark mid-consult, so you can always see that recording is still running.
items.detail: Recording keeps the display on as well as keeping the computer awake. Transcribing and drafting only stop the computer sleeping, so the screen may turn off.

items.name: Computer stays awake until the job is done
items.benefit: A laptop won't go to sleep halfway through a consult, a draft or a model download.
items.detail: Recording, transcribing, drafting and downloading hold a keep-awake lock on Windows, macOS and Linux. If the lock can't be taken, this is logged and the job carries on.

items.name: Draft the note when I stop
items.benefit: Stop recording and the note is already being written by the time Review opens.
items.detail: An option, on by default, in the Recorder side panel and in Settings. Stopping opens Review and starts the draft straight away.

items.name: Visit-type tiles
items.benefit: Pick the kind of visit with one tap, and the right note template is used.
items.detail: Icon tiles for six common visit types (New consult, Recheck, Annual exam, Phone call, Results, Clinician rounds) come first, then the team's own templates. Every other record template is under More types.

items.name: Patient details beside the recorder
items.benefit: Enter the animal, family name and reason for visit while recording, or skip them and add them later.
items.detail: Every field is optional. Details are saved with the visit and time-stamped.

items.name: Import almost any recording
items.benefit: Recordings from phones, dictaphones, browsers, call apps and video files become notes too.
items.detail: WAV (including dictaphone ADPCM), AIFF, MP3, MP2, M4A, MP4, MOV, CAF, FLAC, Ogg, Opus, WebM and MKV are read, using the audio track of a video, and go through the same steps as a live recording. An AAC .m4a encoded from a test consult gave the same transcript as the WAV, and 11 generated formats were transcribed to check them.
items.evidence: engine/os-asr/src/audio.rs (Audio::load); apps/desktop/src/engine.ts AUDIO_EXTENSIONS; docs/guide/recording.md; commits 86d8e1b (m4a from the Windows Media Foundation encoder), 75dc765

items.name: Voice notes and call recordings without extra software
items.benefit: WhatsApp voice notes and recordings from browsers or call apps import without installing anything else.
items.detail: Decoding uses symphonia 0.6.1 and opus-decoder 0.1.1, both written in Rust, chosen over native libopus to keep one native build. It was checked on browser WebM, Ogg Opus, .opus files and WebM video.

items.name: Browser conversion and plain format messages
items.benefit: More file types work in the browser version, and files that can't be read say so plainly.
items.detail: In the browser version, a file the engine can't read (such as HE-AAC) is converted by the browser first. WMA, AMR and Olympus or Philips DSS and DS2 files are refused with a message suggesting the recorder's own converter.

items.name: A failed import leaves nothing behind
items.benefit: A file that can't be read doesn't leave an empty visit cluttering the patient list.
items.detail: If an import fails, its half-made visit folder is deleted. You get a plain message listing the formats that work.
items.evidence: engine/os-app/src/lib.rs import_source ('An import that couldn't be read leaves no empty visit behind'); commit 75dc765

items.name: Notes from recorded phone calls
items.benefit: Turn a recorded call with an owner into a callback note.
items.detail: Record the call with the phone's own call recorder, export the file, import it and draft it with the Phone call template.

items.name: Calls placed from OpenBark
items.benefit: Calls to owners could be placed from OpenBark and charted automatically, without a cloud call service.
items.detail: The design makes OpenBark an extension on the clinic's own phone system, recording each side on its own channel so speaker labels are exact, with a recorded consent announcement. It stays off until configured.

items.name: Dictation and spoken corrections
items.benefit: Vets will be able to dictate a correction over an ambient draft.
items.detail: Dictation and a hybrid mode are in the product brief. 'Dictate correction' in the note editor is listed as not built yet.
items.evidence: the product brief section 2.2; docs/design/STATUS.md 'Not yet'

items.name: Pause and bookmarks
items.benefit: Pause a recording and mark important moments during a consult.
items.detail: The brief asks for pause and resume and 'mark moment' bookmarks. The Recorder design puts bookmarks in the side panel.
items.evidence: the product brief section 5; docs/design/DESIGN.md section 6 Recorder

items.name: Phone recording with the screen locked
items.benefit: A phone in the exam room could record a full consult in the background without going to sleep.
items.detail: A test is designed for iPhone and Android background recording: it must lose no more than 0.5% of audio over a 15-minute locked-screen run, with the transcript written on the phone as it records. It hasn't been run yet.

categories.name: Transcription
categories.intro: Speech becomes text on the clinic's own computer, with silence skipped, speakers separated and misheard veterinary words pointed out.

items.name: Speech recognition on the computer
items.benefit: Consults are transcribed on the clinic's own computer, and no audio is sent anywhere.
items.detail: Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3 runs through sherpa-onnx 1.13.8 and recognises English and 24 other European languages with no setting to change. The standard build is 0.67 GB, and a full-precision build (2.55 GB) is used when the optional NVIDIA speech pack is installed.

items.name: Voice detection
items.benefit: Silence and background noise are skipped, so only speech is transcribed.
items.detail: Silero VAD v6.2.3 finds the speech, and passages longer than 20 s are split. During live recording each utterance is handed on as soon as the pause after it is heard.

items.name: Imports labelled by speaker too
items.benefit: An imported recording gets speaker labels the same way a live one does.
items.detail: Imports run through the live pipeline at full speed with the same speaker tracker. That tracker was more accurate than whole-recording separation on short clips during tuning.

items.name: Hints for misheard drug and condition names
items.benefit: A misheard drug name ('marapitin') gets a visible suggestion (maropitant), and the transcript keeps exactly what was said.
items.detail: Words are compared with the vocabulary by spelling and by sound, with a stricter match for short condition names than for drugs, and hinted words get a dotted underline showing what was heard and the likely term. All 8 hints on the M1 test consults were correct; hints were chosen because biasing the recogniser toward listed terms made Parakeet worse in a test.
items.evidence: engine/os-engine/src/vocab.rs (THRESHOLD_DRUG 0.87, THRESHOLD_OTHER 0.95; test suggests_misheard_drug_names); apps/desktop/src/components/TranscriptList.test.tsx; docs/eval/M1.md finding 3; engine/os-asr/examples/hotwords.rs

items.name: 296-term veterinary vocabulary
items.benefit: The drugs, conditions and procedures clinics say are covered, across small animal, equine, farm and exotics.
items.detail: 168 drugs, 81 conditions, 31 procedures, 8 vaccines, 5 products and 3 routes, including 63 farm, equine, exotics, anaesthesia and suture terms added after ceftiofur came out as 'Seftiapha'. Everyday clinical words such as milligram or vomiting are never hinted.
items.evidence: packages/vocab/veterinary.tsv (296 rows, counted by kind); engine/os-engine/src/vocab.rs COMMON; docs/eval/M2.md 'What the specialty consults found' item 4

items.name: The clinic's own vocabulary
items.benefit: A clinic can add its own drugs, products or terms without changing any code.
items.detail: Terms listed in vocab.tsv in OpenBark's data folder (term, a tab, then the kind) are added to the built-in list. OPENBARK_VOCAB can point to another file.

items.name: Hints for routes and drug names stuck to doses
items.benefit: Common slips such as 'Roman 4' for IV are flagged instead of quietly entering the note.
items.detail: 'Roman 4' gets a hint of likely IV after it happened in three test consults, and a dose stuck to a drug name ('sepromazine.02') is split so both get hints. A first syllable heard as 'a' is rejoined ('a sepromazine' to acepromazine), after a test draft turned acepromazine into xylazine.
items.evidence: engine/os-engine/src/vocab.rs (spoken_form_hints, split_glued_decimals; test iv_heard_as_roman_four_is_hinted); docs/eval/M2.md items 2 and 3

items.name: Hints for misheard pet names
items.benefit: In a multi-pet visit, 'Arlive' is recognised as Olive, so findings go to the right animal.
items.detail: Capitalised words that sound like one of the visit's animals (similarity 0.80 or more) get a name hint that only the note model sees. Ordinary words such as 'alive' are left alone.

items.name: Transcript pane
items.benefit: Follow, scroll and replay the conversation easily.
items.detail: Speaker labels sit in the margin and timestamps on the right, and clicking a line plays the recording from there. Lines the second recogniser heard differently show 'Second listen heard: ...'.

items.name: Transcript follows the recording
items.benefit: During a live recording the newest line stays in view without you scrolling.
items.detail: The list follows new lines until you scroll up, then offers Jump to live. Scrolling stays inside the list, so the page and its controls don't move.
items.evidence: apps/desktop/src/components/TranscriptList.tsx; commit 4dd018e ('The transcript follows new lines without scrolling the page')

items.name: Rename speakers and mark uncertain words
items.benefit: Speakers could be labelled DVM, Client or Tech, and words the recogniser was unsure of could be underlined.
items.detail: Both are in the design and listed under 'Not yet' in the design status.
items.evidence: docs/design/STATUS.md 'Not yet'; docs/design/DESIGN.md section 5 Transcript pane

categories.name: Notes and review
categories.intro: An open model drafts the record on the computer, and the vet reviews it beside the transcript, asks for changes, edits, signs and adds addenda.

items.name: The note is drafted on the computer by Gemma 4
items.benefit: The medical record is drafted by an open model on the clinic's own hardware, with no cloud service.
items.detail: Gemma 4 E2B (3.35 GB), E4B (5.15 GB, the default) and 12B (6.98 GB), all Apache-2.0, run through llama.cpp on the graphics chip where there is one, or on the processor. The context grows with each request up to 32,768 tokens.

items.name: Every draft comes out in the template's shape
items.benefit: Every draft is a complete note under the team's headings, with no free text to tidy up.
items.detail: The note is generated against a structure built from the template, which llama.cpp enforces as the model writes. Every item must cite the transcript lines it came from.
items.evidence: docs/spikes/S2-native-linking.md step 4; docs/adr/0006-templates-from-headings.md Decision 2; engine/os-engine/src/template.rs generate_schema

items.name: Headings written in the template's order
items.benefit: The note is written top to bottom in your template's order, so Subjective comes before Assessment as you would write it.
items.detail: Before, the model wrote headings alphabetically, so it reached the assessment before the history and exam. Measured on 13 test consults: recall about level (141/155 against 143/155), unsupported wording halved (45 to 23) and wrong citations down from 12 to 3.

items.name: Measurements with their units
items.benefit: Every vital sign comes out with the right value and unit.
items.detail: Measurements are written as a value, a unit and the line they came from. Since this change, every numeric vital in the evaluation has come out right with its unit.

items.name: Multi-pet visits: one note per animal
items.benefit: One recording of several animals gives a separate note for each, with no values mixed between them.
items.detail: The model first labels which animal each transcript line is about, then drafts each note only from that animal's lines and the shared ones. On a 7-minute test visit with two cats, facts found went from 17/23 with 6 values in the wrong cat's note to 21/23 with none, at about 6 s more per animal.
items.evidence: engine/os-engine/src/note.rs (attribute_lines, lines_for_pet; test each_animal_drafts_from_its_own_and_shared_lines); docs/eval/M2.md item 2; docs/plans/M2.md item 2

items.name: A tab for each animal
items.benefit: Each animal's note has its own tab in Review and is signed, edited and amended on its own.
items.detail: Add another animal before recording to make a multi-pet visit. If labelling the lines fails, each note is drafted from the whole visit with an instruction to write only about that animal.

items.name: Transcript and note side by side
items.benefit: Check the draft against the conversation and the recording without switching windows.
items.detail: On wide screens the transcript, audio player and note sit side by side, and smaller screens switch to Transcript and Note tabs. The line being played is highlighted.
items.evidence: apps/desktop/src/screens/Review.tsx; apps/desktop/src/app.css (.review-split, max-width 1023px); docs/design/STATUS.md 'Done' sections 4 and 5

items.name: Ask: redraft one heading
items.benefit: Ask for a change to just the Plan, or just the medications, and the rest of the note stays as it was.
items.detail: Ask on any heading opens a panel with suggestions for that heading, and only that heading is redrafted from the transcript. The whole note is then checked again and saved as a new numbered draft with the request recorded.
items.evidence: engine/os-engine/src/note.rs (refine_note; test refine_prompt_covers_only_the_heading); apps/desktop/src/components/RefinePanel.tsx; RefinePanel.test.tsx; docs/adr/0006-templates-from-headings.md Decision 6

items.name: Edit a heading yourself
items.benefit: Type your own correction; it is marked as yours, and a corrected dose doesn't block signing.
items.detail: Editors cover bullet lines, medications (drug, dose, route, frequency, duration) and measurements with units, and each save makes a new draft. Changed lines are marked 'Edited by' with your name, and lines from the recording keep their evidence links.

items.name: Every draft kept
items.benefit: Nothing is overwritten, so you can see how a note changed.
items.detail: Ask, hand edits, reprocessing and drafting again each save a new numbered draft. The earlier drafts stay on disk.

items.name: Draft again with another template
items.benefit: Draft the same consult a different way without recording it again.
items.detail: A template picker in the Review bar offers Draft again and Draft as another template. The model used is shown beside the draft.

items.name: Sign note, and signed notes are locked
items.benefit: A note stays a draft until a veterinarian signs it, and a signed record can't be quietly changed.
items.detail: Sign note records who signed and when. Signed notes refuse edits, Ask and redrafts with 'Add an addendum instead.', and signing twice is refused.
items.evidence: engine/os-engine/src/session.rs (sign_latest_by); engine/os-app/src/lib.rs (generate_note); apps/desktop/src/screens/Review.tsx sign(); docs/plans/M1.md item 6

items.name: Dated, signed addenda
items.benefit: Add later information, like a day-2 phone update, without altering the signed note.
items.detail: Add addendum appends a dated addition signed with your name, and your role when a team is set up. Addenda appear under the note, in copies and in PDFs.

items.name: Check summary under every note
items.benefit: Each draft says how much was checked against the recording and how long it took.
items.detail: It reads '{n} statements, {n} numbers checked against the transcript', with the number of lines the vet entered and 'Drafted in x s'. A notice counts any flagged items.

items.name: Visit details at the top of Review
items.benefit: Reason, species, recording time and how the client consented are shown on every review.
items.detail: A visit details panel with Edit details sits above the note. Consent reads, for example, 'Client agreed out loud; confirmed by Dr Patel, 2026-10-17 20:07'.

items.name: Resizable split and jump keys
items.benefit: Reviewers could resize the panes and jump straight to the lines that need checking.
items.detail: A draggable split remembered on each device, and keys to move between flagged sentences, are listed as not built yet.

categories.name: Accuracy safeguards
categories.intro: Every statement is checked against the transcript, so numbers, findings, citations and patient details that it doesn't support are flagged before a vet signs.

items.name: Core rules no template can remove
items.benefit: However a team customises its template, the rules against made-up content stay in force.
items.detail: Core rules come ahead of every template's own: use only what was said, never write 'normal' unless it was said, copy numbers exactly with units, cite the line each fact came from, and one clinical fact per statement. Teams can add rules and can't remove these.

items.name: Evidence link on every statement
items.benefit: Check any line of the note in a second by hearing the moment it came from.
items.detail: Resting on or focusing a statement lights up its transcript lines. Clicking it, or pressing Enter, plays that moment of the recording.
items.evidence: apps/desktop/src/components/NoteView.tsx; NoteView.test.tsx 'lights the cited transcript lines on hover and plays them on click'; docs/design/DESIGN.md section 1

items.name: Made-up numbers block signing
items.benefit: A number in the draft that isn't anywhere in the transcript blocks signing until the vet fixes it. A number the recogniser misheard can still pass, which is what the optional second listen is for.
items.detail: Every number in the note must appear in the transcript; one that doesn't gets a red callout ('isn't anywhere in the transcript') and Sign note is disabled. It also fails the evaluation and the offline test that runs on every change.
items.evidence: engine/os-engine/src/faithfulness.rs (tests supported_numbers_pass, invented_vital_is_flagged); NoteView.test.tsx 'wraps a number absent from the transcript in a hard-fail callout'; scripts/ci/e2e-offline.sh

items.name: The engine refuses to sign, too
items.benefit: A note with an unsupported number or a citation to a line that doesn't exist can't be signed, even if the screen allowed it.
items.detail: A draft passes only with no unsupported numbers and no invalid evidence links, and the engine refuses to sign any draft that hasn't passed. On screen an invalid link is a softer flag, so the engine is the stricter of the two.
items.evidence: engine/os-engine/src/faithfulness.rs (passed = invalid_evidence.is_empty() && unsupported_numbers.is_empty()); engine/os-engine/src/session.rs sign_latest_by; apps/desktop/src/screens/Review.tsx

items.name: Zero invented numbers on every evaluated consult
items.benefit: On every scripted test consult so far, from wellness visits to euthanasia, the draft contained no number that wasn't in the transcript.
items.detail: M1 reported 0 at every prompt revision across 4 consults, and M2 reported 0 across 9 specialty consults, 3 GP templates and 3 client documents. M0 reported 0 for both E4B and 12B.

items.name: Wrong citations underlined
items.benefit: A correct value linked to the wrong moment of the recording is marked, so the evidence trail stays trustworthy.
items.detail: A number that is in the transcript but not in the lines a statement cites gets an amber dotted underline and a tooltip. M0 measured 5 per note on the paced test consult, which is why it has its own flag.
items.evidence: engine/os-engine/src/faithfulness.rs test number_from_wrong_segment_is_a_citation_mismatch; NoteView.test.tsx 'underlines a value cited to the wrong line'; docs/perf/M0.md safety finding 3

items.name: Missing or unknown evidence caught
items.benefit: Every statement must point to a real moment in the consult.
items.detail: Every cited line must exist in the transcript. Missing or unknown references are reported as invalid evidence.

items.name: Word-level check of each statement
items.benefit: A finding the vet never mentioned, or a dropped 'no' that flips a finding, is flagged even when no number is involved.
items.detail: The important words of each statement must appear in the lines it cites, with negations counted and 152 abbreviation and spoken-form pairs treated as the same (SC and under the skin, PO and by mouth, BID and twice). On the M1 consults it raised 22 flags (13 wrong-line citations, 5 real embellishments and 4 false flags since fixed), and flags ask for a check without blocking signing.
items.evidence: engine/os-engine/src/align.rs (FOLD table, 152 pairs; NEGATIONS; tests invented_claims_are_flagged, supported_and_paraphrased_statements_pass); docs/eval/M2.md item 1; docs/plans/M2.md item 1

items.name: Suggests the right line when a citation is wrong
items.benefit: Instead of only saying a citation is wrong, the app points to where it was actually said.
items.detail: When a flagged statement's words are found elsewhere, up to three lines that together hold at least 75% of them are suggested. The note reads 'It may come from line n'.
items.evidence: engine/os-engine/src/align.rs test wrong_citations_get_a_suggestion; NoteView.test.tsx 'flags a line whose words aren't in its cited line, with the likely line'

items.name: Patient details must have been said
items.benefit: The draft can't guess a species or other detail from a pet's name or the complaint.
items.detail: Species, breed, sex, age and name are checked against their cited line, with synonyms such as dog, canine and puppy understood. This was added after a draft wrote 'Species: dog' for an animal never described.

items.name: Second listen on numbers (optional download)
items.benefit: When the second recogniser is installed, it catches slips like '100 mL' heard as '10 mL' that a transcript-only check could never see.
items.detail: Lines with numbers, hints or one of 31 drug- and condition-like endings (-itis, -osis, -mycin, -pril and 27 more) are recognised again by Whisper large-v3-turbo, and a number that differs is shown as 'The second recogniser heard X instead of Y'. It isn't in the first-run download, so add it from the Models screen; on a 9.6-minute test consult it checked 19 of 57 segments and caught both recognition errors ('10 mL' for 100, '$120' for $320).
items.evidence: engine/os-engine/src/crosscheck.rs (CLINICAL_ENDINGS, 31 entries; tests dropped_magnitude_is_a_disagreement, chooses_segments_that_matter); engine/os-engine/src/models.rs required_status (Whisper turbo not included); engine/os-engine/src/live.rs; docs/eval/M1.md 'Second-opinion recognition'

items.name: Both readings kept, with no extra wait
items.benefit: The second listen never overwrites the transcript. During a live recording it runs in the background, so usually only the last few checks are left when you stop, though a slower computer may take longer.
items.detail: Both readings are kept side by side and the vet decides. During a live recording the second listen runs in the background.

items.name: Terms the second listen heard become hints
items.benefit: If Parakeet writes 'artitis' but the second recogniser hears 'otitis', the reviewer sees the suggestion.
items.detail: When the second recogniser is installed, known veterinary terms that only its reading contains are attached as hints labelled 'second recogniser'. In M1, adding it together with new rules for medications and declined tests raised facts found from 36/44 to 39/44, with 0 invented numbers.

items.name: Spoken numbers read as digits
items.benefit: 'Thirty-nine point two' said aloud and '39.2' in the note are recognised as the same value, so the check is fair and strict at once.
items.detail: 'One hundred and twenty' becomes 120, 'four and a half weeks' 4.5 and 'point seven' 0.7. Both sides are put in one standard form before comparing.
items.evidence: engine/os-engine/src/numbers.rs (tests normalises_spoken_numbers, canonicalises, spoken_then_extracted_matches_note); engine/os-engine/src/crosscheck.rs test spelled_and_written_numbers_agree

items.name: Tooth numbers and times read correctly
items.benefit: 'One oh eight' stays tooth 108, and 'three forty' isn't added up into 43.
items.detail: Digits said one by one ('four oh four') are joined into one number, while 'three forty' stays as two numbers. This was found during the specialty-template evaluation.

items.name: Tenfold dose error guard
items.benefit: A dose said as 'point one milligrams per kilo' can't quietly become 1 mg/kg.
items.detail: Recognition writes 'point one' as '.1', sometimes stuck to the drug ('hydromorphone.1'), and this is always read as 0.1 with a visible hint. Before the fix a test surgery note had 1 mg/kg and the check passed it; it now gives 0.1 mg/kg.
items.evidence: engine/os-engine/src/numbers.rs test a_decimal_without_its_leading_zero_is_still_a_decimal; engine/os-engine/src/vocab.rs test dose_written_without_a_leading_zero_is_hinted; docs/eval/M2.md finding 1

items.name: Misleading hints held back
items.benefit: Condition names get a hint only on a near-exact match, so a misleading suggestion is much less likely.
items.detail: Condition names need a near-exact match: 'artitis' scores 0.948 against arthritis but was really otitis, so no hint is given. The rule is that a missing hint beats a misleading one.

items.name: 'Not discussed' instead of guesses
items.benefit: Sections nobody talked about say so plainly instead of being filled in.
items.detail: Empty headings show 'Not discussed' in the app, in copies and in PDFs, and a medication without details reads 'dose, route and frequency not stated'. Every draft is labelled 'Draft: not reviewed or signed by a veterinarian.'

items.name: Flagged lines marked in copies
items.benefit: Anything that couldn't be matched to the recording stays visibly marked, even after copying.
items.detail: The copied draft says how many items couldn't be matched. Each one is marked '[check against recording]'.

items.name: Requests steer and are never evidence
items.benefit: An Ask request guides the model but never counts as evidence: numbers are checked again and unsupported wording is flagged. The model is told to keep every supported fact, but one test redraft dropped one, so compare the new draft with the earlier one.
items.detail: An Ask request guides the model without counting as evidence, and numbers are checked again afterwards. Every supported fact is kept unless the vet asked to remove it.

items.name: Vet edits listed, never blocked
items.benefit: A vet correcting a dose is never stopped from signing, and their own lines are clearly marked as theirs.
items.detail: Hand-edited items are marked as entered by the vet and listed for review. Unchanged items keep their checks against the recording.

items.name: Specialty safety rules
items.benefit: Each specialty template carries the extra guardrails its risks need.
items.detail: Oncology never calculates a dose or body surface area, production animal leaves withdrawal times empty unless said, and dental keeps Triadan numbers as said. Estimate explanation copies prices exactly and never adds them up.

items.name: Note quality improved only by measurement
items.benefit: Each prompt and schema change was measured for facts found and invented numbers, and changes that hurt were fixed or weighed against other gains.
items.detail: SOAP facts found went 33/44 (75%), 37, 28, 36, 39 and 40/44 (91%) across a baseline and five measured changes, with 0 invented numbers each time; the drop to 28 came when vocabulary hints were first added and was fixed by writing measurements with separate units. After M2 the SOAP template still scores canine 9/10, feline 17/19 and smoke 5/5.
items.evidence: docs/eval/M1.md table (six rows); docs/eval/M2.md ('canine 9/10, feline 17/19, smoke 5/5'); commits 591ad1b, 837f400, f7fbc20

items.name: Safety findings published openly
items.benefit: Known weaknesses are written down with what is done about each.
items.detail: Published findings include 'hundred' dropped in slow speech (now caught by the second listen), misheard drug names (hinted) and wrong citations (flagged). Still-open cases, such as 'ASA one' heard as 'A sat one', are listed too.

items.name: Validation in clinics
items.benefit: OpenBark will be checked in real clinics before it is offered for clinical use.
items.detail: OpenBark is in beta today. Every figure on this page comes from scripted test consults voiced on a computer, or from developer machines.
items.evidence: README.md ('Status: beta ... hasn't been validated for clinical use yet'); packages/eval/fixtures/

categories.name: Privacy and security
categories.intro: Everything runs on the clinic's computer, visit files are encrypted, and every network connection the app can make is listed.

items.name: Everything stays on the computer
items.benefit: Recordings and notes never leave the computer unless you copy or export them.
items.detail: Transcription, drafting and checking run with the network unplugged once the models are downloaded. The sidebar shows 'This device' or 'Web, this computer only'.

items.name: No telemetry, licence server or cloud fallback
items.benefit: Nothing about the clinic or its patients is collected, and nothing phones home.
items.detail: There is no analytics, crash reporting, update check, licence server or fallback to a cloud model.
items.evidence: docs/network.md 'Nothing else at run time'; the product brief section 3

items.name: Every network connection listed, each with an off switch
items.benefit: Clinics and IT can see exactly what OpenBark connects to, when, and how to stop it.
items.detail: There are five, all started by the user: two kinds of model download, the browser version listening on this computer only, Hugging Face search and the optional NVIDIA speech pack. Any other connection is treated as a bug.
items.evidence: docs/network.md (R1 to R5, plus build-time hosts B1 to B6)

items.name: Network guard in every build
items.benefit: Every CI run fails if any Rust part of the app other than the model downloader depends directly on a web-client library.
items.detail: A CI script walks the dependency tree for web-client libraries (reqwest, ureq, isahc, attohttpc, surf). Only the model downloader may use one.

items.name: Browser version reachable only from this computer
items.benefit: The browser version can't be reached from phones or other computers on the network.
items.detail: openbark serve listens only on 127.0.0.1, port 4317 by default. It won't listen on the clinic network until the Clinic Hub adds sign-in and encrypted connections.

items.name: Other websites can't use the browser version
items.benefit: A web page open in another tab can't read or change OpenBark's data through the local browser version.
items.detail: The server answers only requests addressed to itself (which blocks DNS rebinding) and coming from its own pages, and every change must carry an X-OpenBark header that another site can't add. Network and device paths are refused however they are spelled, and the folder browser needs the same header.
items.evidence: engine/os-server/src/lib.rs (Host, Origin and X-OpenBark middleware with tests); commit 3888f20 'Web mode'

items.name: The server enforces licences and downloads
items.benefit: The browser version can't be made to skip a licence or start two downloads at once.
items.detail: Licence acceptance and one download at a time are enforced by the server, as well as on screen. A restart is refused while work is running.
items.evidence: commit 3888f20 ('licence acceptance and a single download enforced by the server, restart refused while busy'); engine/os-server/src/lib.rs

items.name: Access tokens sent only where needed
items.benefit: A Hugging Face token is never sent to other hosts.
items.detail: A token goes only to huggingface.co, and only for a gated model the user chose. Search sends only the search words or the model's name.

items.name: NVIDIA libraries fetched only with consent, and verified
items.benefit: The clinic accepts NVIDIA's licence knowingly, and every downloaded file is checked.
items.detail: NVIDIA's CUDA runtime, cuBLAS and cuDNN are fetched from NVIDIA's own packages after the clinic ticks acceptance, and are never shipped with the app. Every file is pinned by address, size and SHA-256.

items.name: Encryption at rest for every visit file
items.benefit: A copied, backed-up or synced visit folder gives nothing away without the clinic's key. For a lost or stolen computer, turn on BitLocker or FileVault as well.
items.detail: Each file is encrypted with XChaCha20-Poly1305 under a random 256-bit key, with its file name bound in so files can't be swapped. It was checked on 6 older visits migrated and a new import, with no patient names left on disk.
items.evidence: engine/os-engine/src/vault.rs; docs/adr/0008-encryption-at-rest.md; docs/plans/M1.md item 10; docs/versions.md chacha20poly1305 row

items.name: Audio encrypted as it records
items.benefit: A recording is never on disk unencrypted, not even briefly.
items.detail: Audio streams into encrypted 64 KiB chunks of about 2 s each, each bound to its position so chunks can't be reordered. Fixed-size chunks let playback jump to any point.

items.name: Uploads decoded in memory
items.benefit: A recording uploaded in the browser version is never written to disk unencrypted.
items.detail: Uploaded audio is decoded from memory. It goes into the encrypted visit folder as it is processed.
items.evidence: engine/os-app/src/lib.rs import_bytes ('Decoded from memory: the upload never touches the disk unencrypted'); docs/plans/M1.md item 10

items.name: Team list and patient list encrypted too
items.benefit: Staff names, roles, PIN hashes and the patient list are protected like the visits.
items.detail: The team and patient files are read and written only through the encryption module. They use the same data key as the visits.

items.name: Key kept in the system keychain
items.benefit: Normally the encryption key is held by the operating system's keychain. Where there is none, it is kept in a file in the user's OpenBark folder, which is weaker, and Settings says so.
items.detail: The key lives in Windows Credential Manager, macOS Keychain or Linux Secret Service. Where no keychain is available, such as over a remote connection, a key file readable only by the user account is used, and Settings says which is in use.
items.evidence: engine/os-engine/src/vault.rs (KeySource, FILE_WARNING); docs/adr/0008-encryption-at-rest.md Decision 2; apps/desktop/src/screens/Settings.tsx Encryption

items.name: Recovery key for a new computer
items.benefit: Move to a new computer or reinstall without losing access to records.
items.detail: Settings shows the recovery key on request, to print or keep in a password manager, and it can be imported on another computer. Import refuses to replace a different key unless asked, and uninstallers warn to save it before deleting data.
items.evidence: engine/os-engine/src/vault.rs (recovery_key, import_key); engine/os-cli/src/main.rs KeyCommand; docs/adr/0008-encryption-at-rest.md Decision 3; install/README.md

items.name: Encrypt older visits in place
items.benefit: Visits saved before encryption existed can be protected with one button.
items.detail: Settings lists visits saved before encryption with Encrypt them now, which rewrites every file in place. Old plain files stay readable until then.
items.evidence: engine/os-engine/src/vault.rs (encrypt_folder; test folders_encrypt_in_place); engine/os-cli/src/sessions.rs; engine/os-server/src/lib.rs /api/encryption/encrypt-existing; docs/adr/0008 Decision 4

items.name: Playback without plain files
items.benefit: Recordings play back without ever being decrypted to disk.
items.detail: Audio is decrypted into memory for playback, and all clinical reads and writes go through one encryption module. A test guards that no visit file goes around it.
items.evidence: docs/adr/0008-encryption-at-rest.md Decision 5 and Consequences; apps/desktop/src/engine.ts audioUrl

items.name: Forget the key
items.benefit: A clinic retiring a computer can make its encrypted visits unreadable there.
items.detail: The command openbark key forget deletes the key from the keychain and the key file, after a confirmation flag. The visits can then be opened only with the recovery key.

items.name: Encryption tested: nothing plain on disk
items.benefit: Tests show recordings and notes can't be read without the key, even if a recording stops mid-way.
items.detail: Tests cover round trips, a wrong key failing, files bound to their names and audio encrypted as it streams. A saved visit is checked to leave nothing readable on disk.

items.name: Minimal patient list
items.benefit: OpenBark holds just enough about each animal to group its visits.
items.detail: Patient records hold only the animal's name, family name, species and timestamps. There is no medical history or client contact information.

items.name: One-time recording consent notice
items.benefit: Each computer reminds the clinic of its duty to get clients' consent before the first recording.
items.detail: A dialog stays until 'I understand, and I'll get consent from clients before recording' is ticked. It can be shown again from Settings.
items.evidence: apps/desktop/src/components/ConsentNotice.tsx; packages/ui/src/Sheet.test.tsx 'a notice that needs an answer ignores Escape until answered'; docs/guide/getting-started.md

items.name: Optional consent record for each visit
items.benefit: Record how each client agreed, saved with the visit, with the clinic's rule enforced.
items.detail: When switched on, the clinic sets its rule (all parties or one party), a script to read and the method, and each consent is saved with who confirmed it and when. Consent is taken before recording or importing starts, clinician-only consent is refused under an all-parties rule, and 'Client declined' means recording never begins.
items.evidence: engine/os-engine/src/session.rs (ConsentRule, ConsentMethod, Consent::check); apps/desktop/src/components/ConsentStep.tsx; ConsentStep.test.tsx; apps/desktop/src/screens/Recorder.tsx declineConsent; docs/plans/M1.md item 7

items.name: Consent step covers imports too
items.benefit: When consent is recorded for each visit, an imported phone or call recording asks for it just like a live one.
items.detail: Import opens the same consent panel before the file is read. The consent is checked against the clinic's rule and saved with the visit.

items.name: Exports are clearly the only plain copies
items.benefit: Clinics know exactly which copies need handling as medical records.
items.detail: The guide says PDFs and copied text are the only way clinical text leaves OpenBark unencrypted. They should be kept as carefully as any record.

items.name: Optional end-to-end encrypted sync
items.benefit: A vet's notes, templates and settings could follow them across devices without the server being able to read them.
items.detail: The accepted design is opt-in and off by default, encrypted on the device with keys the server never holds, and carries transcripts and notes only: recordings never leave the device that recorded them. It could be self-hosted. It hasn't been built yet.

items.name: Startup passphrase and per-user keys
items.benefit: Clinics could add a passphrase or per-user keys on shared computers.
items.detail: A passphrase protecting the data key can be added as an option. Per-user keys come with Clinic Hub sign-in.

categories.name: Patients and visits
categories.intro: Visits are organised under each animal and linked automatically, with what the clinic typed kept apart from what was said.

items.name: Patients list
items.benefit: Every animal you have seen, most recent first, with a search box to find one fast.
items.detail: One row per animal shows a species icon, visit count, last visit type and date. The list filters by animal or family name.

items.name: Patient page with every visit
items.benefit: See all of an animal's visits and whether each is transcribed, drafted or signed.
items.detail: Each visit shows its type icon, reason, date, length and a status written in words (Transcribed, Draft, Signed). New visit opens the Recorder with the patient filled in.

items.name: Automatic patient linking
items.benefit: Visits group under the right animal with nothing to set up, including older visits.
items.detail: Visits link by animal and family name, ignoring case, spacing and accents, and older visits link themselves the first time patients are listed. A multi-pet visit appears under every animal in it.
items.evidence: engine/os-engine/src/patients.rs (match_key, find_or_create; test records_are_found_by_name_and_family_whatever_the_spelling); docs/adr/0011 Decisions 2 and 3

items.name: Find a patient when recording
items.benefit: Link today's visit to an animal you've seen before in a couple of keystrokes.
items.detail: A search box suggests up to 6 matching patients with species and visit count, and choosing one fills the name, family name and species. Typing a new name makes a new patient.

items.name: Edit details without rewriting history
items.benefit: Correct a name or species while past visits keep what was entered at the time.
items.detail: Patient name, family name and reason for visit are time-stamped when entered and when changed. Editing a patient doesn't alter past visits.

items.name: Clinic-entered details are context, never evidence
items.benefit: Details typed by reception help the model and are never treated as something said.
items.detail: They reach the model marked as entered by the clinic and not evidence. Species decides which species-only headings appear and is never taken from the recording.

items.name: Recent visits table
items.benefit: The day's recordings in one table.
items.detail: Time, patient, reason, template, length, drafts and status. It works by keyboard, and Enter opens a visit.

items.name: Reprocess a visit
items.benefit: Redraft an unsigned visit from its recording, as the same visit type or another one.
items.detail: A button beside each visit on the patient page drafts it again from the same recording, as the same type when a draft went wrong or as another type. Earlier drafts are kept, and signed notes stay final with addenda for anything new.
items.evidence: apps/desktop/src/components/ReprocessSheet.tsx; apps/desktop/src/screens/PatientDetail.tsx; docs/guide/recording.md 'Drafting a visit again'; apps/desktop/e2e/patients.mjs; commit 3888f20

items.name: 11 species
items.benefit: Dogs, cats, horses, farm animals and exotics are all first-class patients.
items.detail: Dog, Cat, Horse, Cattle, Sheep or goat, Pig, Bird, Reptile, Rabbit, Small rodent and Ferret. Six have their own icon (dog, cat, horse, cow, bird, rabbit), and pigs, reptiles, ferrets and unknown species show a paw.

items.name: Merge, split and delete patients
items.benefit: Clinics could fix patients merged by the same name, or carry the practice system's patient number.
items.detail: This is named as a later change if same-name merging becomes a problem. Deleting patients needs its own careful flow.

categories.name: Templates
categories.intro: Twenty ready-made templates, and a builder that lets any team write its own from plain headings without touching code or prompts.

items.name: 20 built-in templates
items.benefit: Ready-made notes for general practice, specialties, farm, equine, exotics and owners from day one.
items.detail: 16 record templates, from SOAP, New consult and Recheck to Dental, Surgery and anaesthesia, Oncology, Exotics, Equine, Production animal and Euthanasia and quality of life, plus 4 client documents. Tests check that each one loads, validates and prints to PDF with all its headings.
items.evidence: packages/templates/*/template.yaml (20 folders); engine/os-engine/src/template.rs test every_builtin_loads_and_its_empty_note_validates; engine/os-engine/src/pdf.rs test every_builtin_template_renders_a_pdf_with_its_headings

items.name: Specialty templates tested on their own consults
items.benefit: Each specialty template was checked on a test consult of its kind, with no made-up numbers.
items.detail: 9 scripted specialty consults found 91 of 98 facts (93%) with 0 invented numbers. Dental 10/10, spay 14/16, hit by car 13/13, equine lameness 11/11, mastitis 9/11, bearded dragon 10/10, atopic dog 8/9, lymphoma 10/11 and quality of life 6/7.

items.name: Templates made from plain headings
items.benefit: A team can build a dental, surgical, exotics or callback template without knowing anything about schemas.
items.detail: A template is headings and subheadings holding bullet points, a text box, measurements with units or medications, with optional plain instructions. The structure the model fills is generated from them, so every team template gets the same evidence links, 'Not discussed' handling and checks.
items.evidence: engine/os-engine/src/template.rs (generate_schema, PartKind; test team_template_from_headings_only); docs/adr/0006-templates-from-headings.md Decisions 1 and 2; docs/templates.md

items.name: Text boxes keep their evidence links
items.benefit: A heading written as a paragraph can still be checked line by line against the recording.
items.detail: The text box writes connected sentences shown as a paragraph. Each sentence still cites its own transcript lines, so the evidence link works inside it.

items.name: Template builder
items.benefit: Build a template in two panes with a live preview, by mouse or keyboard.
items.detail: A structure list with drag handles and Move up and Move down buttons sits beside instructions per heading, icon, level of detail and audience. Delete asks for confirmation, and unsaved changes prompt before leaving.
items.evidence: apps/desktop/src/screens/Templates.tsx Builder; docs/design/STATUS.md 'Done' section 5 Template builder

items.name: Live preview and 'What the model is told'
items.benefit: See the note's shape and the exact instructions the model gets before saving.
items.detail: The preview updates 300 ms after typing stops and checks the template. A second tab shows the exact instructions the model will receive.

items.name: Template from an example note
items.benefit: Paste a note the clinic already writes and get a matching template, with no patient details copied.
items.detail: The model lists the example's headings in the clinic's own words and picks a content kind and instruction for each, and the example (up to 20,000 characters) is never saved. On three test notes it found 4/4, 9/9 and 8/8 headings, copied nothing about the patient and recognised a discharge letter as a client document.

items.name: Example instructions by heading and by practice type
items.benefit: Teams see what a good instruction looks like for their work, instead of a blank box.
items.detail: Team headings get one of 17 example sets matched on the title (dental, lameness, anaesthesia, vaccines, withdrawal times and more), and 8 whole-note examples cover practice types from small-animal GP to shelter and referral. Examples reach the model only when the vet uses one.

items.name: Headings for one species
items.benefit: One template serves dogs and cats: a cat's note asks about FeLV and FIV, and a dog's about heartworm.
items.detail: Any heading can be limited to one of 11 species groups, to dogs and cats, to farm animals or to exotics, and other species' headings are removed before drafting. The same consult entered as a cat and as a dog gave only the right headings.
items.evidence: engine/os-engine/src/template.rs (SPECIES, for_species; test headings_for_other_species_are_left_out_of_prompt_and_schema); apps/desktop/src/species.ts SHOW_FOR; docs/eval/M2.md item 4

items.name: Level of detail and audience
items.benefit: Choose concise, standard or thorough notes, and whether a template is for the record or the owner.
items.detail: Concise asks for the fewest words that keep every fact, and thorough includes every relevant detail said and nothing unsaid. Record templates are signed by a veterinarian, and client templates follow the signed note and are never signed.
items.evidence: engine/os-engine/src/template.rs Detail; engine/os-engine/src/note.rs rules; apps/desktop/src/screens/Templates.tsx builder-meta

items.name: Team standards from one-off requests
items.benefit: A correction a vet asks for once can become how every later note is written.
items.detail: Save as a standard stores an Ask request against a heading or the whole note, and later drafts follow it as a team standard. Each standard shows who added it and when, and can be removed.
items.evidence: engine/os-engine/src/template_store.rs (add_standard; test standards_for_builtin_and_team_templates); engine/os-engine/src/note.rs test standards_reach_the_prompt; apps/desktop/src/components/RefinePanel.tsx; docs/adr/0006 Decision 7

items.name: Try a template on a past visit
items.benefit: Test a new template on a past consult before using it live.
items.detail: Try on a visit lists the last 20 visits. It drafts the chosen one with the template.

items.name: Templates as shareable, versioned files
items.benefit: Share templates between clinics by copying a folder, or keep them under version control.
items.detail: Each template is a template.yaml file in its own folder, and each saved change raises its version. Built-ins are read-only (Duplicate to change them), and a new template never takes over an existing one.
items.evidence: engine/os-engine/src/template_store.rs (tests builtins_are_read_only, save_list_version_and_delete); docs/adr/0006 Decision 4; docs/templates.md 'Files'

items.name: Every draft keeps its own template
items.benefit: Old notes still read correctly after a template changes, and any draft can be reproduced.
items.detail: Each draft saves the template it was written with, standards included. Changing the template later doesn't touch it.

items.name: Template limits and helpful errors
items.benefit: An unfinished or oversized template gets a clear message instead of a broken draft.
items.detail: Templates can hold up to 30 sections, 20 subheadings, 30 fields, 80 headings in all and 1,500 characters of text. A hand-written structure that doesn't match the headings is refused.

items.name: Template icons
items.benefit: Each visit type is recognisable at a glance.
items.detail: A picker offers 39 icons, such as a stethoscope, tooth, horse and syringe. Record notes default to a clipboard and client documents to a speech bubble.

items.name: Dental chart
items.benefit: A tooth chart could be filled from the transcript and edited by click.
items.detail: Being tested: a chart with canine and feline Triadan numbering for missing, fractured and mobile teeth, periodontal stage, extraction and resorption. Each finding links to its transcript line and appears in the note and PDF. It isn't released yet.
items.evidence: docs/plans/M2.md item 7 ('Built, awaiting approval'); docs/adr/0021-dental-chart.md (proposed); docs/design/DESIGN.md section 5 Dental chart

items.name: Summaries of past records
items.benefit: Prior records, including scanned PDFs, could be summarised on the computer and used as context for a new note.
items.detail: The plan reads scanned pages on the computer and links every summary item to its source page. History would count as context and never as evidence.
items.evidence: docs/plans/M2.md item 8 and 'Decisions for the product owner'

items.name: Notes straight from audio (experiment)
items.benefit: A future option could write notes from audio without a separate transcription step.
items.detail: An audio-capable model would run as an experiment. It stays only if it comes within 10% of Parakeet's word error rate.
items.evidence: docs/spikes/S2-native-linking.md configuration C; the product brief section 4.4

items.name: Structured research output
items.benefit: Problem lists, diagnoses and medications could be exported as data for registries and quality review.
items.detail: Optional structured data alongside the written note is one of the product brief's goals.

categories.name: Client documents and export
categories.intro: Handouts for owners that follow the vet's corrected note, plus PDFs and copy formats for any practice system.

items.name: Client documents that follow the vet's note
items.benefit: Discharge instructions and summaries use the vet's corrected doses and spellings, in plain language.
items.detail: Discharge instructions, client summary, estimate explanation and euthanasia aftercare open from buttons under the note, with the evidence link, Copy, Save PDF and Draft again. They are never signed and are labelled 'Draft for the client: check it before handing it over.'

items.name: Estimate explanation and euthanasia aftercare
items.benefit: Help owners understand costs and aftercare, with accurate, gentle wording.
items.detail: Estimate explanation copies prices exactly and never adds them up. Euthanasia aftercare covers arrangements and support in gentle words.

items.name: Medications exact, numbers checked
items.benefit: Owner handouts never paraphrase or recalculate a dose, and drug names are spelled right.
items.detail: Client documents give medications exactly as in the note and write doses in digits, after a test discharge listed 'Marapitin' and doses in words. They go through the same invented-number check, with numbers the vet entered counting as supported.

items.name: Client documents in the client's language
items.benefit: A discharge can go home in French from a consult held in English.
items.detail: Each document's language, any of the 7 note languages, is chosen in its panel. A French discharge from an English consult kept the medication and every number unchanged.

items.name: PDFs with the clinic's letterhead
items.benefit: Signed notes and client handouts print as clean PDFs ready to file or send.
items.detail: PDFs carry the clinic's letterhead, visit details, the signature or a clear draft line, every heading, addenda and page numbers, on Letter or A4. The same output comes out on every platform, and citations are left out so it reads cleanly.
items.evidence: engine/os-engine/src/pdf.rs (note_pdf, PageSize; tests every_builtin_template_renders_a_pdf_with_its_headings, long_notes_flow_onto_more_pages); docs/plans/M1.md item 12

items.name: Copy into any practice system
items.benefit: Paste the whole note, or one heading, cleanly into whatever practice software the clinic uses.
items.detail: Copy as plain text (most practice systems), formatted text or Markdown, with an optional header, addenda and transcript line numbers. Each section has its own Copy button.

items.name: Practice system integration
items.benefit: Notes could go straight into ezyVet, Instinct, Shepherd, Digitail and others.
items.detail: Planned: a browser extension for web-based practice systems, an ezyVet connector, clipboard presets for desktop systems, and HL7v2 and FHIR R4 exports.

categories.name: Team
categories.intro: Several people can share one computer, each in their role, with a record of who did what on every note.

items.name: Team members, roles and PINs
items.benefit: Vets, technicians and reception each do what their role allows, and only veterinarians can sign.
items.detail: Veterinarians can do everything, technicians record, draft and edit, and reception records and enters patient details; the engine enforces these roles. PINs of 4 to 8 digits are stored as salted hashes with 100,000 rounds, and the first member must be a veterinarian.
items.evidence: engine/os-engine/src/users.rs (Role, ROUNDS; test team_members_roles_and_pins); apps/desktop/src/components/TeamSettings.tsx; docs/plans/M1.md item 11

items.name: Quick switch between staff
items.benefit: Staff pick their name and enter their PIN to take over the computer.
items.detail: A 'Who's using OpenBark?' picker with Switch sits at the bottom of the sidebar. The last veterinarian can't be removed while others remain.

items.name: Change your own PIN
items.benefit: Staff can change their PIN themselves without asking a veterinarian.
items.detail: Settings has 'Change my PIN'. A veterinarian resets someone else's PIN by removing and re-adding them.

items.name: Who did what, on every draft
items.benefit: The record shows who recorded, drafted, edited, asked for changes and signed each note.
items.detail: Each visit stores who recorded it, and each draft who drafted, edited or asked for it. Each signature and addendum records who made it, with their role.

items.name: Roles stated plainly in the guide
items.benefit: Clinics know what team roles protect against and what they don't.
items.detail: The user guide says roles keep an honest record on a shared computer and aren't a security boundary against someone with access to the computer's account. Clinic-wide accounts and audit come with the Clinic Hub.

items.name: Solo mode
items.benefit: Working alone needs no team setup.
items.detail: With no team set up, the app runs for one person. Your name in Settings is saved with each note you sign.

items.name: Clinic Hub
items.benefit: One clinic computer could serve phones and thin laptops across the clinic network.
items.detail: Planned: discovery on the clinic network, pairing by QR code, encrypted connections, a shared clinic store, an audit log and an admin dashboard. It would stay off unless Hub mode is switched on.
items.evidence: the product brief sections 4.7 and 6 (M4); docs/network.md 'Planned' M4

categories.name: Languages
categories.intro: Consults in 25 languages, notes in 7, the interface in 5, with the limits stated plainly.

items.name: Consults in 25 European languages
items.benefit: Consults can be held in English or 24 other European languages with no setting.
items.detail: Parakeet TDT v3 recognises the language automatically. Nothing needs to be chosen before recording.

items.name: Notes in seven languages
items.benefit: Write the record in the clinic's language whatever language the consult was in.
items.detail: Notes can be written in English, French, Spanish, German, Portuguese, Italian or Dutch, with drug names, doses, units and numbers kept exactly as said. When the note's language differs from the consult's, the word-level check is switched off and the number check still runs.

items.name: App in five languages
items.benefit: Staff can use the interface in English, French, Spanish, German or Portuguese.
items.detail: Each of the four translations holds 745 strings, and the app starts in the browser's language when available, falling back to English. The translations were machine-generated and are waiting for review by native-speaking veterinary staff.

items.name: PDF labels in five languages
items.benefit: The fixed words on a PDF, such as Patient, Signed by and Page 1 of 2, match the clinic's language.
items.detail: Labels come in English, French, Spanish, German and Portuguese. Anything missing falls back to English.

items.name: Translation integrity tests
items.benefit: Translated screens never lose names, dates or values from their text.
items.detail: Tests check that every translation keeps the English placeholders and that English fallback works. The build scripts check placeholders too.

items.name: Built-in headings stay in English
items.benefit: A clinic writing notes in another language knows to rename its headings.
items.detail: Headings come from the template, so built-in headings stay in English whatever the note language. A French clinic can duplicate a template and rename its headings.
